I am 75 years old. My hands know this land. I have been planting wheat and corn on these fields since I was a young man, just like my father did, and his father before him. In Quzhou, that is what we do — wheat in the cold months, corn in the hot months. Same fields, same rotation, every year. I do not need a book to tell me this.

My land is about 5 mu. I cannot manage more at my age. My knees are bad and my son helps during the harvest.

For wheat I will plant in October after the autumn rains soften the ground. I buy seed from the supply station in town — the kind they sell there, improved seed, not the old grain I saved myself like we used to do. I gave that up years ago because yields were getting low. I will plow and rotary-till the field before planting, the way I always do. I water four times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading, once when the grain is filling. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then spread urea in spring when the wheat wakes up. I spray twice — once for weeds in autumn, once in spring for the rust and aphids that always come.

For corn I plant right after the wheat comes off in June, no time to waste. I do not plow for corn — I just open a furrow and drop the seeds. Hybrid seed only, that gives the best ears. Summer rain handles most of the water but I run the pump twice if it is dry. Corn does not need as much spraying but I go once for the borer worm.

I do not try new things at my age. I know what this land gives me. I keep doing what works.
